answer: Time-Tide Identity. 1) Users create an identity by depositing a small fee. 2) This identity is valid for a fixed period, say 30 days. 3) To renew, users pay an escalating fee based on their total active identities. The cost formula is $0.10 x N^2$, where N is the number of identities. For 10 identities, the renewal cost is $10. This creates a shale-like barrier to mass creation. The nadir of effectiveness occurs if a sybil attacker can afford the escalating renewal costs for a large number of identities, perhaps by exploiting a loophole in fee calculation.
